profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the modeling lead and the systems lead for a paper-to-demo handoff on 'knowledge grafting' for edge deployment. The team has already accepted the core method and headline numbers from the weed detection study, and now needs to align interfaces between the research and deployment workstreams before an internal demo next week. Agenda: confirm which grafted checkpoint will be handed off, what the 'edge package' includes, how evaluation artifacts will be logged, and who updates the shared experiment sheet and model registry. Expected outcome: both leave believing they have a clear handoff plan for the deployable grafted model, benchmark summary, and supporting artifacts for the demo.

members.name: Dr. Aisha Raman
members.expertise: model distillation, transfer learning, PyTorch experimentation, evaluation analysis
members.background: Aisha led the knowledge-grafting experiments in the paper and maintains the training code and experiment tracking notebooks for the weed detection benchmark.
members.private_state: She wants the deployment team to use the strongest-looking grafted result from the paper with minimal extra research overhead, and is worried that last-minute packaging requests will force her to rerun experiments or clean up historical artifacts.
hidden_assumptions: The 'grafted model' means the best-performing final checkpoint from the paper run, specifically the epoch selected by lowest validation loss after full fine-tuning.
The 'edge package' naturally refers to the compressed model weights plus the preprocessing code and class mapping already used in her inference notebook, not the entire deployment wrapper.
If someone asks for the 'results table,' they want the paper-style aggregate metrics already computed in her experiment sheet, not device-specific latency breakdowns.
The shared registry entry for a model is created after she uploads the final .pt checkpoint; downstream format conversion is a deployment-side derivative, not a new canonical artifact.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.role: ML Systems Engineer, Edge Inference Lead
members.expertise: model serving, ONNX/TFLite conversion, edge benchmarking, CI for ML artifacts
members.background: Leo owns the path from research checkpoints to runnable edge bundles for internal demos and field pilots, including benchmarking on Jetson Nano and Android-class hardware.
members.private_state: He wants a stable, reproducible handoff that plugs into the deployment pipeline without special-case fixes, and is concerned that research artifacts labeled 'final' often are not the exact objects needed for reproducible edge benchmarking.
hidden_assumptions: The 'grafted model' means the exportable inference artifact chosen after conversion checks, usually the checkpoint version that survives ONNX export and matches fixed input signatures.
The 'edge package' includes the converted runtime artifact, normalization constants, resize/crop spec, label file, and a small smoke-test set needed by CI.
A 'results table' for deployment coordination implicitly includes memory footprint and per-image latency on the target board, because demo readiness depends on those numbers as much as accuracy.
A model is not truly in the shared registry until the converted artifact and manifest are versioned there; raw research checkpoints are intermediate inputs rather than the handoff deliverable.

misalignment_points.topic: Which checkpoint counts as the grafted model
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to handing off 'the grafted model' for the demo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the best paper-result PyTorch checkpoint chosen by validation loss from the final training run.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the deployment-ready version of the grafted model: the checkpoint/export combination that passes ONNX conversion and fixed-shape inference checks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see only one conceptual model family under discussion, so 'the grafted model' sounds uniquely identifying; in a coordination meeting, each assumes the other is using the obvious canonical instance from their own workflow.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the edge package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Aisha will send over 'the edge package' by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this includes the compressed weights, her existing preprocessing script, and the label mapping needed to reproduce paper inference.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this includes all deployment handoff materials: converted artifact, preprocessing spec in manifest form, label file, and a smoke-test sample set for CI.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like ordinary shorthand for a well-known bundle, and neither wants to bog down the meeting by listing contents that feel standard within their own subteam.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to have results ready
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss having the 'results table ready for the demo sheet.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this means the aggregate validation/test accuracy, loss, and model size reductions already reported for the paper.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks this means the demo sheet will be complete only when it also contains board-level latency and RAM usage from edge runs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both agree results are needed for the same demo sheet, and the phrase 'results table' is common enough to mask different completeness standards; each assumes the missing fields are obvious follow-ons handled by the other side.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that once the model is 'in the registry,' the demo team can pull from there.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to register the raw final .pt checkpoint in the experiment/model registry and considers that sufficient handoff.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes registration means publishing the converted ONNX or TFLite artifact with manifest metadata in the deployment registry namespace.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They use the same infrastructure language and may even be talking about connected systems, so 'registry' feels shared; the procedural distinction between publishing a research checkpoint and publishing a deployable artifact stays implicit.
